grammar_tips.title: Formal Passive Structures
grammar_tips.explanation: Use the passive voice to focus on research processes. E.g., 'Data were collected from five universities.'

grammar_tips.title: Hedging Language
grammar_tips.explanation: Use modal verbs and cautious language to avoid overgeneralizing. E.g., 'The results suggest...' or 'This may indicate...'

speaking.question: Describe the main steps in publishing a peer-reviewed article.
speaking.answer: You submit a manuscript, it is peer-reviewed, possibly revised, and finally published.

speaking.question: Explain why the abstract is important in journal articles.
speaking.answer: The abstract helps readers quickly understand the article’s main ideas and findings.

speaking.question: Discuss how to avoid plagiarism in academic writing.
speaking.answer: To avoid plagiarism, always cite your sources and use your own words.

speaking.question: Summarize the difference between methodology and results sections.
speaking.answer: The methodology explains how the research was done; the results show what was found.

speaking.question: Give one reason why peer review is valuable.
speaking.answer: Peer review improves the quality and reliability of published research.
